content: Ganciclovir is an antiviral medication primarily used to treat herpes infections of the eye. While it effectively inhibits the growth of the herpes virus, it does not cure the infection, as the virus remains dormant in the body between outbreaks. This medication is specifically designed for herpes-related eye infections and is not effective against bacterial eye infections or other types of eye conditions. To apply ganciclovir eye drops, first wash your hands thoroughly. Avoid wearing contact lenses during an active eye infection or while using this medication. Tilt your head back, look upward, and gently pull down the lower eyelid to create a small pouch. Hold the dropper directly above the eye and place one drop into the pouch. Close your eyes gently and press one finger at the inner corner of your eye (near the nose) for 1 to 2 minutes to prevent the medication from draining out. Avoid blinking or rubbing your eyes after application. Do not rinse the dropper, and if you are using other eye medications, wait at least 5 minutes between applications. For optimal results, use this medication regularly and at the same times each day. Continue the full course of treatment as prescribed, even if symptoms improve after a few days. Common side effects include temporary blurred vision and mild eye irritation or redness. These effects are usually short-lived. Serious allergic reactions to ganciclovir are rare. If you experience any unusual or severe symptoms, contact your doctor immediately. Before using ganciclovir, inform your doctor if you are allergic to it, valganciclovir, or any other substances. This product may contain inactive ingredients that could cause allergic reactions or other issues. Temporary blurred vision may occur after application, so exercise caution when performing activities that require clear vision. During pregnancy, ganciclovir should only be used if absolutely necessary, as its effects on fetal development are not fully understood. It is also unknown whether this medication passes into breast milk, so breastfeeding is not recommended during treatment due to the potential risk of serious adverse effects in nursing infants. Drug interactions may alter the effectiveness of ganciclovir or increase the risk of side effects. Keep a list of all medications and supplements you are taking and share it with your doctor or pharmacist. If an overdose occurs, seek immediate medical attention or contact a poison control center. Store ganciclovir at room temperature and protect it from freezing. Properly discard expired or unused medication as instructed by your healthcare provider. Always follow your doctor’s instructions and attend all scheduled medical and laboratory appointments to monitor your condition and response to treatment.
